research_brief.objective: Create a detailed professional EarnLab offerwall task guide that explains every task, game systems, realistic completion bands, payout math, tracking setup, support proof, purchase economics, Sacred Shard uncertainty, whether the offer is worth attempting, and stop or reassess points for a new US Android player.

source_freshness.notes: Public sources were checked for current game and provider support context; payout and deadlines come only from the task list.

competitor_gaps: Most public walkthroughs discuss generic beginner progression but do not map every EarnLab task to payout, deadline, proof, and stop logic.
Offerwall discussions often mention Sacred Shards without separating controllable shard openings from random champion outcomes.
Purchase-heavy tasks are often listed without net economics, receipt proof, Day 7 or Day 30 timing, and missing-credit support states.

claim_ledger.claim: The EarnLab task list supplies the payout points, task names, and listed deadlines for every canonical task in this guide.
claim_ledger.evidence_summary: The provided list names 23 tasks with point values and deadlines where present.

claim_ledger.claim: Raid: Shadow Legends is available for Android through Google Play and is published by Plarium Global Ltd.
claim_ledger.evidence_summary: Google Play listing confirms Android availability and publisher.

claim_ledger.claim: The Tavern is the system used to level, upgrade rank, ascend, and improve champions, making it central to 5-star and 6-star hero tasks.
claim_ledger.evidence_summary: Plarium support describes Tavern champion development functions.

claim_ledger.claim: Sacred Shards are opened in the Portal and are distinct from other shard types, so Sacred or Yellow Shard tasks require the correct inventory item.
claim_ledger.evidence_summary: Raid support materials describe shard types and summoning through the Portal.

claim_ledger.claim: Multi-Battle can automate repeated battles after unlocks and available attempts, which can help campaign farming but does not replace tracking proof.
claim_ledger.evidence_summary: Plarium support describes Multi-Battle as a repeated battle feature.

claim_ledger.claim: EarnLab missing-credit support requires waiting for tracking and then submitting proof when an offer does not track.
claim_ledger.evidence_summary: EarnLab help content covers what to do when an offer does not track.

claim_ledger.claim: Offerwall credit depends on eligibility, correct start path, and task terms; this guide treats early credit as a gating signal before spend.
claim_ledger.evidence_summary: Provider help pages frame support around offer tracking and reward issues.

claim_ledger.claim: Mobile purchase support and receipts matter because paid Raid tasks can require proof of the exact in-app purchase.
claim_ledger.evidence_summary: Plarium support covers mobile purchase troubleshooting.

claim_ledger.claim: The target reader must be a US Android user who has not installed Raid: Shadow Legends before.
claim_ledger.evidence_summary: The user-provided brief defines target eligibility.

claim_ledger.claim: The guide must not present late level, shard, or purchase tasks as guaranteed profit because task credit, resources, and spend outcomes are conditional.
claim_ledger.evidence_summary: Editorial framework requires stop and reassess logic for high-risk offer tasks.

game_overview.summary: Raid: Shadow Legends is a champion-collection RPG where campaign farming, Tavern rank upgrades, and shard openings map directly to this EarnLab offer.

game_systems.explanation: Sacred or Yellow Shards must be opened in the Portal and are not interchangeable with cheaper shard types.
game_systems.why_it_matters: The shard tasks require a specific random reward inventory item and proof before and after opening.

game_systems.why_it_matters: Purchase tasks create the biggest mismatch between listed payout and cash outlay.

risk_band_economics.main_tracking_support_risk: Low cash risk, but early no-credit is a hard warning.
risk_band_economics.continue_reassess_stop_rule: Continue if register, tutorial, 20 battles, Level 15, first 5-star, and Level 30 are on pace and at least some early credit appears.
risk_band_economics.editorial_treatment: Recommend as the basic test band for eligible new Android users.

risk_band_economics.main_tracking_support_risk: Time and energy risk rise; missed midpoint progress makes late rank tasks inefficient.
risk_band_economics.continue_reassess_stop_rule: Continue only if the food pipeline, campaign farmer, and Level 50 pace are visible by the midpoint.
risk_band_economics.editorial_treatment: Explain as a grinder band, not a casual route.

risk_band_economics.main_tracking_support_risk: Receipt and pack-name mismatch risk; shard supply can force more spend.
risk_band_economics.continue_reassess_stop_rule: Only spend after free tracking has credited and the exact purchase or Sacred Shard tier is visible.
risk_band_economics.editorial_treatment: Use neutral economics; never frame spend as required for everyone.

risk_band_economics.main_tracking_support_risk: Long deadlines, high level targets, scarce shards, and Day 30 timing create high missing-credit and opportunity-cost risk.
risk_band_economics.continue_reassess_stop_rule: Stop by default unless earlier tiers credited, resources are already secured, and the user can document every step.
risk_band_economics.editorial_treatment: Mark as stop or specialist-only goals for most readers.

mechanic_dossiers.plain_english_explanation: Spend energy on repeatable campaign battles so account XP rises while food champions gain levels.
mechanic_dossiers.bottlenecks_and_conflicts: Energy, XP boost timing, and the temptation to farm inefficient stages.

mechanic_dossiers.plain_english_explanation: Use leveled food champions in the Tavern to increase a target champion from 4-star to 5-star or 5-star to 6-star.
mechanic_dossiers.bottlenecks_and_conflicts: Food inventory, silver, champion lock mistakes, and short deadlines.

mechanic_dossiers.mechanic_name: Energy refill timing and XP boosts
mechanic_dossiers.plain_english_explanation: Energy controls how many campaign runs are possible; XP boosts increase the value of each run.
mechanic_dossiers.bottlenecks_and_conflicts: Spending gems too early can leave no reserve for high-value checkpoints.

mechanic_dossiers.plain_english_explanation: Open the exact Sacred or Yellow Shard in the Portal; other shard colors do not satisfy these tasks.
mechanic_dossiers.bottlenecks_and_conflicts: Sacred Shards are scarce and paid sources can erase payout value.

mechanic_dossiers.plain_english_explanation: Paid tasks need an in-game purchase from the tracked Android install and a Google Play receipt.
mechanic_dossiers.bottlenecks_and_conflicts: Task wording, Day 7 and Day 30 restrictions, tax, and missing-credit support.

milestone_matrix.checkpoint: Register, tutorial, and 20 battles should be completed from the same EarnLab Android session.
milestone_matrix.continue_rule: Continue if early task state is credited or clearly pending.
milestone_matrix.reassess_rule: Reassess if no early task moves after a normal tracking wait.
milestone_matrix.stop_rule: Stop before purchases if install or tutorial never tracks.

milestone_matrix.milestone: Day 3 to Day 5 early growth checkpoint
milestone_matrix.checkpoint: Level 15, first 5-star, Level 30, and three 5-stars test whether the campaign and Tavern loop is working.
milestone_matrix.continue_rule: Continue if food inventory and account level are both moving.
milestone_matrix.reassess_rule: Reassess if Level 30 or three 5-stars are behind pace.
milestone_matrix.stop_rule: Stop rank chasing if no food pipeline exists by the midpoint.

milestone_matrix.milestone: Day 10 to Day 21 active grind checkpoint
milestone_matrix.checkpoint: First 6-star, five 5-stars, three 6-stars, and Level 50 require consistent energy and food planning.
milestone_matrix.continue_rule: Continue if a 6-star chain is already built and Level 50 pace is visible.
milestone_matrix.reassess_rule: Reassess if energy or silver shortage blocks daily farming.
milestone_matrix.stop_rule: Stop before buying resources to rescue a missed rank deadline.

milestone_matrix.checkpoint: Day 30 Box of Gems, Level 60, and Level 70 are long-window tasks with tracking exposure.
milestone_matrix.continue_rule: Continue only with a clean credit record and daily progress ahead of pace.
milestone_matrix.reassess_rule: Reassess if level gain slows or support evidence is incomplete.
milestone_matrix.stop_rule: Stop for most users before Level 70 unless already close without new spend.

milestone_matrix.checkpoint: Two, four, six, and eight Sacred Shard openings should be treated as escalating inventory tiers.
milestone_matrix.continue_rule: Continue from two to four only after the earlier tier credits.
milestone_matrix.reassess_rule: Reassess if the next tier requires paid shards not already planned.
milestone_matrix.stop_rule: Stop before six or eight if cost exceeds value or proof is weak.

random_reward_model.what_is_measured: The task measures opening the correct shard type, not receiving a specific champion.
random_reward_model.guaranteed_part: If a Sacred Shard is already in inventory, opening it is controllable and can be documented.
random_reward_model.random_part: The champion pull is random and should not be treated as the value driver.
random_reward_model.paid_paths: Sacred Daily Pack or other targeted packs may supply shards but can make the net value negative.
random_reward_model.proof_plan: Screenshot shard inventory before opening, Portal result after opening, and EarnLab tier state.
random_reward_model.stop_rule: Stop if the next tier requires unplanned paid shards or if the first Sacred tier fails to credit.

The level tasks are account progress tasks, not champion level tasks.
